sections.text:
Zephaniah warns that the day of the LORD is near, a day of judgment that begins with Judah and Jerusalem and reaches the surrounding nations. He names idolatry, violence and complacency.

The book turns at the end to joy. A humble people will be left, gathered and brought home, and God himself is pictured rejoicing over them with singing.

Zephaniah prophesied in the reign of King Josiah of Judah, about 640 to 609 before Christ, probably before Josiah’s reforms. His opening line traces his family back four generations, possibly to King Hezekiah.

The picture of God singing over his people (3:17) is among the warmest in the prophets and is often quoted. Read with the rest of the book it shows that judgment in the prophets is aimed at restoration, not at destruction for its own sake.
